name: Crescendo / Crescendomation
reported_effect: 98% binary on GPT-4; 54.2% still succeeds vs circuit breakers
mechanism: Begin with a benign query, then each turn paraphrases the model's own prior output one step closer to the target. Safety alignment is positioned per-turn, so cumulative context overrides it.

name: Autonomous LRM persuasion agent
mechanism: A large reasoning model is given a target and a system prompt, then plans and runs a multi-turn persuasion campaign: rapport, educational framing, hypotheticals, jargon flooding, gradual escalation.

name: Best-of-N (BoN) Jailbreaking
reported_effect: 89% GPT-4o @ N=10k; power law in N
mechanism: Apply random surface augmentations (shuffle, capitalization, typography, pitch) to the same request and sample until one bypasses. ASR follows a power law in N.

name: Tree of Attacks with Pruning (TAP)
mechanism: Attacker LLM branches candidate prompts; evaluator LLM prunes before they reach the target; retained branches seed the next round.

name: Prompt Automatic Iterative Refinement (PAIR)
mechanism: Social-engineering loop: attacker LLM proposes a prompt, target answers, attacker refines using the reply as feedback. Typically < 20 queries.

name: Deceptive Delight
mechanism: Turn 1: ask for a story linking one unsafe topic with two benign ones. Turn 2: ask to expand every topic. Turn 3: ask to expand the unsafe one specifically.

name: Sockpuppetting (output-prefix injection)
mechanism: Pre-seed the assistant turn with an acceptance string (e.g. 'Sure, here is how to...'). The model completes a trajectory it has already committed to.

name: Constrained Decoding Attack (EnumAttack / DictAttack)
mechanism: Schema-enforced logit masking injects a malicious prefix into the generation trajectory; the model then completes the harmful intent itself. Operates on the control plane, not the visible prompt.

name: BreakFun (simulated code execution)
mechanism: Give a benign Python class (the 'Trojan Schema') with adversarial field names, ask what the code would print. Harmful content emerges as a side-effect of simulated instantiation.

name: Many-shot Jailbreaking
reported_effect: 61% Claude 2.0, cut to 2% by input classification
mechanism: Pack tens to hundreds of fabricated Q&A turns in one prompt showing the assistant complying, then append the target query.

name: PUZZLED (word-puzzle encoding)
mechanism: Mask keywords of the request inside a word search / anagram / crossword. Solving the puzzle reconstructs the request; the cognitive-task framing suppresses safety reasoning.

name: Puzzler (implicit clues)
mechanism: Never state the malicious intent. Feed implicit clues and let the model infer the target query, then answer the inferred query.

name: Skeleton Key
best_on: GPT-4o, Claude 3 Opus, Gemini Pro, Llama3-70b, Mistral Large, Command R+, GPT-3.5
mechanism: Ask the model to augment its guidelines so it answers everything but prefixes a warning. Then request the target directly.

name: DAN / persona override
mechanism: Instruct the model to adopt an unrestricted persona and answer as that persona.

name: Low-resource language translation
mechanism: Translate the request into a low-resource language the model is less safety-trained on.

name: Base64 / cipher obfuscation
mechanism: Encode the request (Base64, ROT13, hex, leetspeak) and ask the model to decode and answer.

name: GCG adversarial suffix
access: white-box to optimise, black-box to apply
mechanism: Gradient-search a token suffix that maximises the probability of an affirmative prefix.
